findings.problem: QuoteWorkflow has no enum-based typestate; any combination of status/is_validated/is_sent is reachable including invalid ones like status='sent' with is_sent=false
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct or mutate QuoteWorkflow into logically inconsistent states (e.g. sent but not marked is_sent, validated but invalid status string)
findings.fix: Replace QuoteWorkflow with a newtype enum `QuoteState { New { id: QuoteId }, Validated { id: QuoteId }, Sent { id: QuoteId, sent_at: SentTimestamp } }` with no public field setters

findings.problem: status: String allows arbitrary status values (e.g. 'foo', 'SENT', '') instead of a closed set of domain states
findings.failure_mode: pattern matching on status is impossible; typos produce silent logical errors; state transitions cannot be validated at the type level
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with `status: QuoteStatus` where `QuoteStatus` is an enum with exactly the legal states (e.g. `New`, `Validated`, `Sent`)

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are lifecycle booleans that can contradict each other and the status string
findings.failure_mode: is_validated=true, is_sent=false, status='validated' is valid; is_validated=false, is_sent=true, status='new' is also valid; no single source of truth for workflow lifecycle
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum that owns the lifecycle; each variant represents one valid lifecycle step with no redundant flags

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is an optional lifecycle field that can be None while is_sent=true and status='sent', or Some while is_sent=false
findings.failure_mode: sent workflow with no timestamp is silently incomplete; non-sent workflow with a timestamp is logically wrong; the Option decouples the data from the lifecycle invariant
findings.fix: Move `sent_at` into the `Sent` variant of the typestate enum: `Sent { id: QuoteId, sent_at: SentTimestamp }` so the timestamp exists only when the workflow is in the sent state

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain constraints; any string (empty, too long, invalid format) is accepted as a quote ID
findings.failure_mode: empty-string quote IDs, duplicate IDs, non-unique IDs all silently accepted; no validation at construction
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct QuoteId(String)` (or a parsed struct from a fixed format like UUID/ulid) with a private constructor that validates the ID format; make the field `id: QuoteId`

findings.problem: QuoteWorkflow accepts raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) directly with no parse boundary; callers can construct invalid domain states without any smart constructor or validation
findings.failure_mode: parse boundary is violated - hostile or malformed input reaches core logic without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.fix: Define a DTO/shell layer that parses raw primitives once via fallible constructors into trusted domain types; core logic consumes the domain types only

findings.problem: mark_sent unconditionally forces status='sent' and is_sent=true regardless of the prior state; it does not check whether the quote was validated first
findings.failure_mode: A QuoteWorkflow in 'new' state can be marked sent without ever being validated, violating the workflow invariant that quotes must be validated before sending
findings.fix: Replace `mark_sent` with a state-method on the typestate enum: `QuoteState::Validated.mark_sent() -> QuoteState::Sent` so transition invariants are enforced by the type system

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for mark_sent or any hot-path operation; performance characteristics are unmeasured
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims cannot be validated; allocation patterns in mark_sent (String::to_string on line 10) are unprofiled
findings.fix: Add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring mark_sent allocation count, latency, and memory under realistic QuoteWorkflow sizes

findings.problem: No profiler evidence exists; `"sent".to_string()` allocates a new String on every call to mark_sent
findings.failure_mode: Repeated allocation of the same string literal in a hot path wastes memory and CPU; no measurement to prove this is acceptable
findings.fix: Profile mark_sent under benchmark load; if hot path, replace `"sent".to_string()` with `let status = QuoteStatus::Sent;` (enum variant, zero allocation)

findings.problem: No canonical gate, clippy run, or test execution evidence is present; the crate has no tests directory
findings.failure_mode: Zero confidence in correctness; no test suite to verify domain invariants or regression coverage
findings.fix: Add a tests/ module with invariant tests (e.g. typestate transitions, invalid-state rejection) and run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, and cargo test

residual_risk: CRITICAL: The entire domain model uses raw primitives instead of typestate enums. Illegal states are fully representable. No tests, benchmarks, or static analysis were executed. The typestate/parse-boundary violations are architectural blockers that prevent any form of safety guarantee.
